title: India Thrash Korea 63-31 to Stay Unbeaten at Asian Games
excerpt: A day after routing hosts Japan, India's kabaddi men dominated South Korea 63–31 in Nagoya to make it two wins from two in their title defence at the 2026 Asian Games.
body:
• India crushed South Korea 63–31 in their second Group A match at the Tokai Citizens Gymnasium in Nagoya on Tuesday, staying unbeaten at the 2026 Asian Games.
  • Captain Sunil Kumar's side led 34–14 at half-time, driven by 38 raid points against Korea's 23, 17 bonus points, and three All-Outs.
  • The win follows Monday's 49–24 rout of hosts Japan, putting India firmly on course to top the group as they chase a ninth men's kabaddi gold in ten editions.
  • India next face Bangladesh on September 23, then Chinese Taipei on Thursday in their final group game.

Two games, two routs

India's kabaddi title defence is off to a ruthless start. After routing hosts Japan 49–24 in Monday's opener, the Indian men's team beat South Korea 63–31 in their second Group A fixture at the Tokai Citizens Gymnasium on Tuesday, keeping their unbeaten record intact at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.

Captain Sunil Kumar's side took early control and never released it. India's raiding unit, stocked with familiar faces from the Pro Kabaddi League, was clinical from the opening exchanges, and the defence backed it up with a string of successful tackles that repeatedly broke up Korea's attacking rhythm.

"Captain Sunil Kumar's side took early control and never released it."

How the rout unfolded

The pattern was set in the first half. India raced to a 34–14 lead at the interval, built on 23 out points and seven bonus points in the opening 20 minutes alone, with two All-Outs that Korea had no answer for. Korea's raiders managed just 10 touch points before the break, unable to find gaps in India's defensive line.

The second half followed the same script. Korea showed marginally more fight after the restart but never threatened a comeback. India added 29 more points, inflicting a third All-Out and stretching the bonus-point tally to 17 for the match. Korea responded with 17 points of their own — nowhere near enough to dent the deficit.

The final numbers underline the gulf: India's raiders picked up 38 out points across the match against Korea's 23, and the defence's tackle success kept Korea's scoring raids to a trickle throughout.

A legacy on the line

India are the most successful kabaddi nation in Asian Games history by a distance, with 11 gold medals from the 13 titles contested. The men have won eight of the nine editions they have played, the lone blemish the bronze at Jakarta 2018 — a defeat that still stings in Indian kabaddi circles and one this squad is plainly intent on avenging with interest.

This campaign is about more than gold. It is about reasserting a dominance that briefly slipped. Two matches, two 30-plus-point margins: the message to every other team in the competition is already clear.

What's next

India return to the mat against Bangladesh on Wednesday, September 23, and close out the group against Chinese Taipei on Thursday. Topping the group would set up the most favourable semifinal path. Meanwhile, the women's team — who opened their campaign with a win over Bangladesh on Monday — take on Iran in their second Group A match on Wednesday.

nri_angle: Kabaddi is India's indigenous sport, and the men's ruthless title defence at the Asian Games — watched by a global diaspora — is one of the purest Indian success stories on the continental stage.
